Lithium Therapy

which complication, and what to doIs this toxicity, diabetes insipidus, hypothyroidism or an expected effect?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Drug script
Bottom line
  • Coarse tremor, ataxia, slurred speech ↑ level toxicity: stop lithium IV isotonic fluids; hemodialysis for altered mental status, seizures, a life-threatening dysrhythmia or a level past the cutoffs in Urgent risks
  • ↑ sodium dilute urine after years of use nephrogenic diabetes insipidus: restore volume; stop lithium if possible
  • ↑ TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) ↓ free thyroxine add levothyroxine; keep lithium going
What it is

Mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder

Mechanism

Handled like sodium; the kidney is its only real exit

Thiazide, NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug), ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor or ARB (angiotensin receptor blocker) more lithium reabsorbed level rises

Narrow therapeutic range

Used for

Acute mania: first line, alone or with an antipsychotic

Bipolar maintenance (linked to lower suicide risk) bipolar I depression, both first line

Kidney disease: valproate for maintenance instead

Risks

Toxicity nephrogenic diabetes insipidus hypothyroidism Ebstein anomaly in pregnancy (LMNOP)

Insights

Collecting duct: lithium blunts the signal of ADH (antidiuretic hormone) fewer aquaporins desmopressin barely changes the urine

Lithium enters collecting-duct cells through the epithelial sodium channel; amiloride blocks that entry, so it can treat the diabetes insipidus when lithium must continue

Adverse effects, by systemroutine effects and complications
Nervous systemFine tremor is routine; coarse tremor, slurred speech, ataxia or drowsiness suggest toxicity; seizures and worsening mental status when severe
GutMetallic taste and diarrhea are common
KidneyPolyuria and thirst are common; long-term use is linked to chronic tubulointerstitial nephropathy
ThyroidHypothyroidism may develop in about 25% (up to 50%), usually within 1 to 2 years of starting
2Urgent risks
ToxicityToxicity: findings commonly appear >1.5 mmol/L

If lithium toxicity (↑ level) brings altered mental status, seizures or a life-threatening dysrhythmia, choose hemodialysis, whatever the level.

LevelLevel >5.0 mmol/L, or Hemodialysis cutoffs>4.0 mmol/L with impaired kidney function (creatinine >2.0 mg/dL); >2.5 mmol/L with prominent signs of toxicity, such as tremor, fasciculations or confusion. In practice: toxicology guidance recommends dialysis >4.0 mmol/L only with impaired kidneys, and only suggests it >5.0 mmol/L.

If any one of these is present, choose hemodialysis.

IngestionRecent large ingestion; alert, kidneys working, level ≤2.5 mmol/L
Activated charcoal does not bind lithium

If no dialysis criterion is met, choose IV isotonic fluids and serial levels.

Water lossDrowsy and volume-depleted with diabetes insipidus
Dehydration also raises the lithium level

If sodium is ↑ and the urine dilute, choose volume replacement and a lithium level.

PregnancyFirst-trimester exposure: Ebstein anomaly

If exposure fell in the first trimester, choose fetal echocardiography.

3Differential
Which effect is it, most tempting first
EffectFingerprintDecides it
Thirst, polyuria; confusion with dehydrationYears of use; ↑ sodium with dilute urine; little or no desmopressin response
Tiredness, cold intolerance, mental fogginess; constipation, myalgias, bradycardia Not the statinMyalgias can come from a statin; constipation, a slow pulse and tiredness typically do not.Usually within 1 to 2 years; ↑ TSH with ↓ free thyroxine, or TSH >10 μU/mL
Routine side effectsFine tremor, polyuria, metallic taste, mildly ↑ TSHSodium, mental status, level and free thyroxine all normal
Chronic toxicity In a vignetteAsked as: Addition of which of the following medications most likely contributedLong-term user; new thiazide, NSAID, ACE inhibitor or ARB, or dehydrationNeurologic findings lead; ↑ level (after a thiazide it usually rises within 10 days)
Acute toxicityRecent large ingestionSoon after ingestion: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea often come first; ↑ level
Obesity with polyuria suggests glucose diuresis↑ glucose; urine not dilute (solute diuresis)
Primary polydipsiaPolyuria with dilute urine; especially common in psychiatric patientsSodium usually ↓, not ↑; urine concentrates >600 mOsm/kg after water deprivation
Polyuria with dilute urineDesmopressin clearly raises urine osmolality
Hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia↑ calcium on routine labsYears of lithium; ↑ calcium on the yearly check, then ↑ PTH (parathyroid hormone)
LMNOP
  • L – lithium
  • M – movement: tremor
  • N – nephrology: kidney injury and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (thirst, heavy urination)
  • O – hypothyroidism
  • P – pregnancy: Ebstein anomaly
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext best step
Thirst and polyuria plus confusionWater loss, not the routine polyuriaSodium with urine osmolality, plus a lithium level
Mildly ↑ TSH beside ↑ sodium and dilute urineA decoy: the thyroid explains neitherRead the sodium against the urine; also check free thyroxine
Pause point
Years of lithium: a mildly ↑ TSH, confusion, a high sodium Offered as hypothyroidism, or the confusion as acute toxicity The optionsAcute lithium toxicity: confusion and trouble walking fit toxicity; but the labs here point to the kidney.
Lithium-induced hypothyroidism: the TSH of 5.5 is mildly high; but no free thyroxine is given, and hypothyroidism explains neither the hypernatremia nor the dilute urine.
Routine side effects of lithium: polyuria alone is routine; but with dehydration, confusion, hypernatremia and dilute urine, this can be life-threatening.
Type 2 diabetes mellitus: a body mass index of 29 with polyuria suggests glucose diuresis; but hypernatremia after years of lithium fits the kidney better.
Down to two: lithium-induced diabetes insipidus or hypothyroidism. Diabetes insipidus: 20 years of lithium, thirst and polyuria, then a sodium of 150 with urine osmolality 200; the kidney is losing water it should keep. With no lithium level and no mention of diabetes insipidus in the stem, the answer comes from reading the sodium against the urine. Four of the five options are effects of lithium; the one tempting lab, a mildly high TSH, points to the wrong effect. Hypernatremia with dilute urine after years of use → The kidney

Check a level too, since water loss can raise it.

7Treatment
1

1st linetoxicity with nausea, diarrhea, a coarse tremor, ataxia, slurred speech or an unsteady gait; mental status intact, level 2.5 or under, no dialysis criterion met

Stop lithium; IV isotonic fluids; serial levels
2

Escalatealtered mental status, seizures, a life-threatening dysrhythmia, or a level past the cutoffs in Urgent risks

Hemodialysis
Manage by effect
EffectDoAvoid
Stop lithium if possible, then restrict salt. If lithium must continue, amiloride may be used instead of salt restriction, since a low-sodium diet would raise the levelA thiazide, or an NSAID other than aspirin or sulindac, without close levels: both raise the lithium level
HypothyroidismAdd levothyroxine; continue lithiumStopping lithium: thyroid changes are not a reason
8Follow-up
Monitoring
  1. Before startingBaselines: creatinine, BUN (blood urea nitrogen), TSH, calcium with albumin
  2. Day 7First level
  3. Every 1 to 2 weeksLevel, until stable in range
  4. Every 6 to 12 monthsLevel, electrolytes, creatinine, BUN, TSH
  5. YearlyCalcium with albumin; PTH if calcium is ↑
WhenCheckWhy
Before startingCreatinine, BUN (blood urea nitrogen), TSH, calcium with albumin; weight, height, blood pressure; a pregnancy test when relevant Guideline detailWith cardiac disease or cardiac risk factors, or in older adults, add an ECG before startingBaselines for kidney, thyroid and calcium effects; teratogenic risk
After startingLevel at 7 days, then every 1 to 2 weeks until stable in rangeNarrow range: the dose is titrated to the level
Every 6 to 12 monthsLevel, electrolytes, creatinine, BUN, TSHKidney and thyroid effects build over time
YearlyCalcium with albumin; PTH if calcium is ↑Long-term use is linked to hyperparathyroidism
↑ TSH, normal free thyroxineRecheck in 4 to 6 months; add levothyroxine once free thyroxine falls or TSH >10 μU/mL; a trial is reasonable if symptoms appearNot a reason to stop lithium

Levels are troughs, about 12 hours after the last dose. Target In practice:Guidelines split the target: acute mania 0.8 to 1.2 under age 65; maintenance 0.6 to 1.0, some using 0.8 as the floor (= mmol/L); toxic >1.5.

Interactions
WithEffectDo
Thiazide diureticLevel usually rises within 10 daysLevel and creatinine more often
NSAIDRaises the level (more is reabsorbed); aspirin and sulindac are exceptionsLevel and creatinine more often
ACE inhibitor or ARBRaises the levelLevel and kidney function more often
MetronidazoleCan raise the levelCheck the level
Dehydration, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, low-sodium dietRaise the levelCheck the level; consider a lower dose with infection, heavy sweating or diarrhea
Practice
  1. 59-year-old man with bipolar disorder, on lithium 8 years lisinopril started 2 weeks ago 4 days of nausea and a coarse tremor of both hands alert and oriented HR 64/min · BP 126/80 mm Hg · sodium 139 mEq/L → Serum lithium level and creatinine → an ACE inhibitor raises the lithium level; coarse tremor and nausea suggest toxicity
  2. 44-year-old man with bipolar disorder, stable lithium 6 years 3 days of vomiting and diarrhea drowsy; oriented to person only coarse tremor, slurred speech, unsteady gait HR 56/min · sodium 138 mEq/L · creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (baseline 0.9) · urine osmolality 520 mOsm/kg → Chronic lithium toxicity → dehydration raised the level in a long-term user, and neurologic findings lead; a serum lithium level confirms
  3. 22-year-old woman took 30 immediate-release lithium tablets 2 hours ago started lithium 3 weeks ago vomited 3 times; diarrhea alert, oriented; no tremor HR 96/min · BP 116/70 mm Hg · lithium 2.2 mmol/L · creatinine 0.8 mg/dL → IV isotonic fluids and serial lithium levels → alert, kidneys working and level under 2.5 mmol/L: no dialysis criterion is met; lithium does not bind charcoal
  4. 67-year-old man on lithium for 15 years a week of poor intake; took extra tablets yesterday drowsy, confused; responds only to a loud voice coarse tremor HR 54/min · BP 100/62 mm Hg · lithium 4.4 mmol/L · creatinine 2.9 mg/dL (baseline 1.1) → Urgent hemodialysis → decreased consciousness, or a level over 4.0 mmol/L with impaired kidneys: either one indicates dialysis; lithium does not bind charcoal
  5. 62-year-old woman with bipolar disorder, stable lithium dose for 9 years hydrochlorothiazide started for hypertension 3 weeks ago now coarse tremor, slurred speech, confusion HR 60/min · lithium 2.4 mmol/L · creatinine 1.0 mg/dL → Increased renal reabsorption of lithium → a thiazide increases renal reabsorption of lithium, which is handled like sodium; the kidney is its only real exit
  6. 54-year-old man on lithium for 10 years for bipolar disorder knee osteoarthritis pain; asks what to take for it euthymic, alert and oriented BP 128/80 mm Hg · creatinine 1.0 mg/dL · lithium trough 0.8 mmol/L → Oral naproxen, taken daily → NSAIDs raise the lithium level
  7. 46-year-old man on lithium for 14 years 6 months of thirst passing large volumes of urine day and night euthymic, alert and oriented BP 124/78 mm Hg · sodium 146 mEq/L · glucose 94 mg/dL · urine osmolality 160 mOsm/kg → Collecting duct unresponsive to antidiuretic hormone → lithium blocks the ADH (antidiuretic hormone) signal, so fewer aquaporins reach the membrane; desmopressin changes the urine little or not at all
  8. 58-year-old woman on lithium for 16 years months of thirst and polyuria in bed 2 days after a fall now drowsy and disoriented HR 104/min · BP 102/64 mm Hg · sodium 156 mEq/L · urine osmolality 140 mOsm/kg · creatinine 1.3 mg/dL → IV fluid replacement and a serum lithium level → water and volume loss from nephrogenic diabetes insipidus; dehydration also raises the lithium level; the drowsiness fits a sodium of 156, and the level is not yet known, so replace volume and measure it
  9. 33-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder, euthymic on lithium for 18 months 2 months of tiredness and feeling cold small nontender goiter alert and oriented HR 62/min · TSH 12.4 μU/mL · free thyroxine low · sodium 140 mEq/L · lithium trough 0.8 mmol/L → Add levothyroxine and continue lithium → lithium-induced hypothyroidism; thyroid abnormalities are not a reason to stop lithium
  10. 26-year-old man, lithium for 4 months; euthymic mild tremor holding a cup urinating more than before alert, oriented, gait normal HR 72/min · sodium 140 mEq/L · urine osmolality 480 mOsm/kg · TSH 5.6 μU/mL · free thyroxine normal · trough 0.9 mmol/L → Expected lithium adverse effects → normal sodium, mental status, level and free thyroxine; a fine tremor, polyuria and a mildly high TSH are routine
  11. 40-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder, euthymic on lithium for 3 years takes no other medications routine visit; last laboratory studies 12 months ago alert and oriented BP 118/74 mm Hg · BMI (body mass index) 23 kg/m² → Lithium level, creatinine, TSH and calcium → level, electrolytes, creatinine and TSH every 6 to 12 months; calcium yearly
  12. 61-year-old woman on lithium for 12 years for bipolar disorder 4 days of loose stools and a new tremor; drops her keys 1 week ago started hydrochlorothiazide, omeprazole and lovastatin Not dehydrated; sodium normal wide-based gait · lithium 1.9 mEq/L → Hydrochlorothiazide → a thiazide decreases sodium reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule, so more sodium and lithium are reabsorbed in the proximal tubule; omeprazole and lovastatin leave kidney function and sodium clearance unchanged
Pairs with Polyuria: the renal workup of a dilute urine and the agent used when lithium must continue. Teratogenic Exposures: lithium in pregnancy. Thyroid Disease in an Adult: reading the TSH.
Transferable rule

When a patient on a drug with several known complications presents, choose the complication that explains every abnormal value. On lithium, a high sodium with dilute urine belongs to the kidney, and a mildly high TSH beside it is not the answer.
